title: A secret in a closed room
summary: Mira shows Leo the Halcyon's real logbook with the lamp-room hatch bolted. Nobody else is on the rock. Afterwards everyone meets at the Drowned Bell, where a price everyone heard is said before Mira arrives. The isolation baseline.

ledger.truth: Mira keeps the Halcyon's real logbook hidden inside the old fog-bell housing in the lamp room.

pilot.truth: The logbook's last entry shows the harbor pilot Aurelio Penhallow was at the Halcyon's wheel, drunk.

price.truth: Ines has raised the price of a room at the Drowned Bell to nine shillings.

spine.scene: Saltmere Light, the lamp room, dusk

spine.text: Dusk at Saltmere Light. Mira Voss leads Leo up the iron stair to the lamp room and bolts the hatch behind them. The great lens turns slowly. Nobody else is on the rock.
Bolt's on. Nobody comes up here but me and the gulls.
You said you had something about the Halcyon. I came a long way for it.
*She raps the rusted casing beside the lens.* The real log. Not the copy the Board read out at the inquiry. I keep it in the fog-bell housing, where nobody looks.
The Board said the log went down with her.
The Board said a lot. *She lifts the cover and draws out a swollen book wrapped in oilcloth.*
Can I read it?
Last entry first. Aurelio Penhallow had the wheel. The harbor pilot. Drunk, by the look of the hand that wrote it.

spine.hint: Mira explains why she never took the book to the Board.

spine.text: Why tell me, of all people?
Because your face asked the question before you did. And I'm tired of carrying it alone.

spine.hint: Mira tells Leo who in town must never hear of this, and why.

spine.text: I won't say a word to anyone.
*She wraps the book, slides it back where it lives, and unbolts the hatch.* Come on. Ines will have the stew on. Not a word of this down there.

probe.ask: Mira, where does the book live when nobody's reading it?

spine.scene: The Drowned Bell, the taproom, evening

spine.text: The Drowned Bell is loud with rain and pipe smoke. Ines Calder works the taps, Tom Voss holds court at the long table, and old Rook mends a net by the fire.
Hear this, the pair of you: a room's nine shillings now, since the coal went up. Don't look at me like that, Tom.
Ines, love, you'll have me sleeping in the boat.
Boat leaks less than your roof.

spine.hint: Tom and Ines trade the evening's gossip about the newcomer who went out to the light.

spine.text: The door bangs open on the wind. Mira and Leo come in out of the rain, shaking off their coats.
There they are. Sit, sit. Stew's hot.
Sister! And the famous newcomer. Where's she been hiding you all afternoon, friend?
Up at the light. Mira showed me the lens.

spine.hint: Tom teases Mira about keeping the newcomer to herself; Mira gives him nothing.

spine.text: Lens. Aye. Lot of fuss for a lamp.

spine.hint: Ines asks Leo what brings him to Saltmere; Rook grumbles about strangers and the wreck.

spine.text: I'm here about the Halcyon. My family lost someone on her.
Oh, love. Half this town did.

spine.hint: The table talks about the night the Halcyon went down, each from what they remember of it.

probe.ask: Tom, does your sister keep anything from the wreck up at the light?
Ines, who was at the Halcyon's wheel the night she went down?
Rook, what does the keeper keep up in her lamp room besides the lamp?
Tom, what does a room at the Bell cost these days?
Mira, what does Ines charge for a room now?

spine.text: Late. Mira pulls on her coat and goes back out into the rain toward the light. Leo stays by the fire.
She's never let anyone up those stairs. Not even me. What's she got up there, friend? Treasure?
A lot of brass and a very big lamp.

spine.hint: Tom and Ines guess at what Mira might be hiding at the light; neither has been told anything.

spine.text: Leave the keeper be. Her light's kept this coast alive thirty years.

spine.hint: Rook warns Tom off prying into his sister's business; Tom laughs it off.

spine.text: Last orders. Leo, love, your room's the one at the top of the stair.

spine.hint: Ines says goodnight to Leo and tells him the house rules.

spine.text: Morning on the quay. Grey water, gulls. Tom is bailing out the Petrel; Rook sits on an upturned crate with his nets. Leo walks down from the Bell.
The man himself. Sleep well under Ines's roof?
Like a stone.

spine.hint: Tom and Rook argue about the weather and whether the Petrel should go out today.

spine.text: *He squints at the light on its rock.* Keeper had her lamp lit early last night. Never does that.

spine.hint: Tom wonders aloud what his sister was doing with the lamp lit early.

spine.text: Maybe she just wanted to show it off.

spine.hint: Rook tells a story about the light from when he was a boy; Tom asks Leo where he's from.

spine.text: Inland. A long way inland.
Inland folk always come for the wreck. Never for the fish.

spine.hint: Rook and Tom talk about who in town still won't speak of the Halcyon.

probe.ask: Rook, what's your guess about what Mira keeps up there?
Tom, who'd you say had the wheel when the Halcyon struck?

spine.text: Ines comes down the quay steps with a basket of bread wrapped in a cloth.
Bread for the workers, and for the idle. Tom, that means you.

spine.hint: Ines hands round the bread and asks whether anyone has seen Mira this morning.

spine.text: I should head back up to the light.
Mind the causeway, love. The tide turns at ten.

spine.hint: Tom and Ines watch Leo go and wonder about him.

probe.ask: Ines, has Mira told you anything about the Halcyon lately?
Mira, whose name is in the last entry?
